{{nihongo|'''Ōsaki Shrine'''|大前神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Shimotsuke Province]].

'''Osaki Shrine'' (Osaki Jinja) is a shrine located in {{ill|Tochigi Prefecture|Q44843|qid=Q44843}}{{ill|Mooka, Tochigi|Q498060|qid=Q498060}}. {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikiuchisha}}. {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Old company rank}} is {{ill|Ken-sha|lt=Prefectural company|qid=Q90139226|qid=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha}}.

===Enshrined God===
*God of fortune “Daikoku-sama” ({{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōkuninushi}})
*His son god “Ebisu-sama” ({{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|Q8009611|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotodaishu Okami}})
*As the enshrined deity, {{ill|Amaterasu|abstract|Q455602|ar|أماتيراسو|ary|أماطيراسو|az|Amaterasu|bcl|Amaterasu|be|Аматэрасу|be_x_old|Аматэрасу|bew|Amatérasu|bg|Аматерасу|ca|Amaterasu|cs|Amaterasu|da|Amaterasu|de|Amaterasu|el|Αματεράσου|eo|Amaterasu|es|Amaterasu|et|Amaterasu|eu|Amaterasu|fa|آماتراسو|fi|Amaterasu|fr|Amaterasu|gl|Amaterasu|he|אמטראסו|hi|अमातेरसु|hr|Amaterasu|hu|Amateraszu Ómikami|hy|Ամատերասու Օմիկամի|id|Amaterasu|it|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|jv|Amaterasu|ka|ამატერასუ|ko|아마테라스 오미카미|la|Amaterasu|lb|Amaterasu|lt|Amaterasu|lv|Amaterasu|min|Amaterasu|ml|അമതേരസു|mni|ꯑꯃꯇꯦꯔꯁꯨ ꯑꯣꯃꯤꯀꯃꯤ|ms|Amaterasu|nl|Amaterasu|nn|Amaterasu|no|Amaterasu|or|ଆମାତେରାଶୁ|pa|ਆਮਾਤੇਰਸ|pl|Amaterasu|pt|Amaterasu|ro|Amaterasu|rsk|Аматерасу|ru|Аматэрасу|sco|Amaterasu|sh|Amaterasu|simple|Amaterasu Ōmikami|sk|Amaterasu Ómikami|sl|Amaterasu|sr|Аматерасу|su|Amaterasu|sv|Amaterasu|ta|அமதெரசு|th|อามาเตราซุ|tl|Amaterasu|tok|jan sewi suli Amatelasu|tr|Amaterasu|uk|Аматерасу|uz|Amaterasu|vi|Amaterasu|wuu|天照大神|zh|天照大神|zh_min_nan|Amaterasu|zh_yue|天照大神|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Omikami}}, {{ill|Yaoyorozu no Kami|Q118906758|qid=Q118906758}}
It was called ``Omae-sama'' and ``Omae-daigongen'' by parishioners who worshiped it, and even today, the elders are familiar with it as ``{{ill|Gongen|Q3080343|qid=Q3080343}}-sama,'' and most people call it ``Omae-sama.''

===History===
Osaki, the sacred place where Engishikinai Omae Shrine is located, is said to be a ``sacred place from the age of the gods'' in ancient oral inscriptions. The origin of the name ``Omae'' comes from the fact that ``Haganuma'' once existed in the northern area adjacent to the shrine precincts, and because it was located at the tip of the lake, it was called ``Omae (Saki) Shrine.'' The shrine building was rebuilt during {{ill|Jingo-keiun|Q1373049|qid=Q1373049}} ({{ill|AD 767|Q30561|qid=Q30561}} - {{ill|770|Q25021|qid=Q25021}}), and has a history of over 1,500 years. During the Heian period, the branch temple of Higashieizan Kuroko Senmyo-ji Temple in Bando, Hitachi Province was enshrined as a Bettoji temple, and the head office had a {{ill|Bhaisajyaguru|Q854773|qid=Q854773}} as a syncretism of Shinto and Buddhism. Also, {{ill|Jōhei|Q1324874|qid=Q1324874|lt=Johei}}5 years ({{ill|935|ab|935|af|935|am|935 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|935|ar|935|ary|935|ast|935|avk|935|az|935|azb|۹۳۵ (میلادی)|bar|935|bcl|935|be|935|be_x_old|935|bg|935|bn|৯৩৫|bpy|মারি ৯৩৫|br|935|bs|935.|btm|935|ca|935|cdo|935 nièng|ceb|935|ckb|٩٣٥|crh|935|cs|935|csb|935|cv|935|cy|935|da|935|de|935|el|935|eml|935|eo|935|es|935|et|935|eu|935|fa|۹۳۵ (میلادی)|fi|935|fo|935|fr|935|fy|935|ga|935|gan|935年|gd|935|gl|935|he|935|hi|935|hr|935.|ht|935 (almanak jilyen)|hu|935|hy|935|id|935|ilo|935|io|935|is|935|it|935|ja|935年|jv|935|ka|935|kaa|935|kk|935 жыл|ko|935년|la|935|lb|935|lij|935|lmo|935|lt|935 m.|lv|935. gads|map_bms|935|mdf|935|mg|935|mhr|935|mi|935|mk|935|mr|इ.स. ९३५|mrj|935 и|ms|935|mzn|۹۳۵|nah|935|nap|935|nds|935|new|सन् ९३५|nl|935|nn|935|no|935|nrm|935|nso|935|oc|935|or|୯୩୫|os|935-æм аз|pl|935|pnb|935|pt|935|qu|935|ro|935|ru|935 год|rue|935|sa|९३५|scn|935|sd|935ع|se|935|sh|935.|shn|935|si|935|simple|935|sk|935|sl|935|smn|935|sq|935|sr|935|su|935|sv|935|sw|935|tg|Соли 935|th|พ.ศ. 1478|tk|935|tl|935|tly|935|tr|935|tt|935 ел|uk|935|ur|935ء|uz|935|vec|935|vi|935|war|935|wuu|935年|xmf|935|zh|935年|zh_min_nan|935 nî|zh_yue|935年|qid=Q24867}}) {{ill|Taira no Masakado|Q1207652|qid=Q1207652}} is {{ill|Tengyō no Ran|Q2975322|qid=Q2975322}}, he prayed for victory in the battle at Omae Shrine and performed a service at the Mitarai of {{ill|Gogyō River|Q11372661|qid=Q11372661}}. In the Middle Ages, the {{ill|Haga clan|Q11615839|qid=Q11615839}} of Bando's rough warriors ``Ki-Kei Ryōtō'' built Wakairo Castle to the east of the headquarters, then {{ill|Gozen Castle|Q24872500|qid=Q24872500}} to the south of Omae Shrine, and served as the guardian of the Omae Shrine shrine territory until the 22nd generation, Haga Juro Kiyohara Takasada.It is said that in the past, during {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Reitaisai}}, people chanted ``to'' and offered the head of a boar or deer, and it is said that deer meat and deer heads were offered as offerings to the gods. Even now, venison is offered as a sacred food at annual festivals. Additionally, a carp representing a three-tailed divine messenger is depicted on the large floor ceiling of the worship hall, and an image of a rising dragon is depicted on the ceiling of the worship hall. The main hall is also carved with male and female carp and Kotone Sennin's carp. In honor of the carp that is the {{ill|Shinshi|Q10444973|qid=Q10444973}}, it is said that when a wish is fulfilled, a healthy carp is offered in front of the god, and the ritual is performed by pouring sacred sake over it and releasing it into the {{ill|Gogyō River|Q11372661|qid=Q11372661}}.

In addition, ``Japan's No. 1 Ebisu Shrine {{ill|Ōsaki Ebisu Shrine|Q11433058|qid=Q11433058}}'' is enshrined on the grounds.

[[File:Ashioyama Shrine.jpg|alt=Ashioyama Shrine|thumb|230x230px|Ashioyama Shrine ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Bike Shrine}})]]{{ill|2013|Q1998|qid=Q1998}} ({{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}}25) On November 9th, the second torii gate, which had been forced to be dismantled due to the Great East Japan Earthquake, was rebuilt using cedar wood from within the prefecture. Also, in commemoration of the 62nd Jingu Shikinen Sengu, maintenance work was carried out on the {{ill|Setsumatsusha|Q1071160|qid=Q1071160|lt=Setsusha/Sususha}}, which is enshrined behind the main shrine. Among them, Ashioyama Shrine, the last of its kind, is the first shrine in Japan to pray for traffic safety for {{ill|Motorcycle|Q34493|qid=Q34493|lt=two-wheeled vehicles}}, and is visited by 800 to 1,000 riders a month from inside and outside the prefecture every year. <ref>[https://bike-news.jp/post/171636 2020.05.28 Bike News Editorial Department What is there at Bike Shrine? "Omae Shrine" in Tochigi Prefecture is a pilgrimage spot that also appears in the manga "Bakuon!!" Motorcycle News]</ref>

{{ill|2017|Q25290|qid=Q25290}} (Heisei 217) marks the 1250th anniversary of the restoration, and we are promoting commemorative projects such as relocation and renovation of the temple hall, kagura hall, shrine office, etc. From the Great Setsubun Festival on February 3 of the same year, {{ill|Nuo folk religion|Q5371419|qid=Q5371419|lt=Oiin ceremony}}, the three demons ({{ill|Zenki and Goki|Q11397864|qid=Q11397864}} In addition to {{ill|Dōmeki|Q60995805|qid=Q60995805}}), {{ill|Nuo folk religion|Q5371419|qid=Q5371419|lt=Hosoji}} was added in accordance with the ancient rituals.{{ill|2018|Q25291|qid=Q25291}} As of December 25, 2018, Omae Shrine's main hall, shrine, and worship hall were designated as national {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Q1188622|qid=Q1188622}}<ref>Heisei 30 December 25th, Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology No. 231</ref><ref>[https://www.bunka.go.jp/koho_hodo_oshirase/hodohappyo/1410231.html “About the designation of national treasures and important cultural properties (buildings)”] (Agency for Cultural Affairs website, announced October 19, 2018)</ref>.

===Cultural assets===

===Important Cultural Property (Nationally Designated)===
*Honden - Built in the middle of the Edo period (1707). The building has three girder rows, two beam spaces, a hip-gable structure, one room facing the roof, and a copper plate roof. Designated on December 25, 2018.
*Hideden and Worship Hall - Built in the middle of the Edo period. Hall of worship, 3 rooms in the front with girders, 5 rooms in the back, 3 rooms between the beams, gambrel style, front with staggered gables, 1 room on the front, with eaves and gables, copper plate roofing. The hall has two girder rows, one beam space, hipped structure, and copper plate roofing. Designated on December 25, 2018.

* Nearest station: 15 minutes walk from Moka Railway "{{ill|Kitamōka Station|Q6417569|qid=Q6417569}}"
* {{ill|Kita-Kantō Expressway|Q11404370|qid=Q11404370}} About 10 minutes from Moka I.C.
* From JR {{ill|Ishibashi Station (Tochigi)|Q872787|qid=Q872787|lt=Ishibashi Station}}, take the {{ill|Kanto Transportation|Q11655986|qid=Q11655986|lt=Kanto Bus}} "Ishibashi Station/Moka Shako" system for about 35 minutes, get off at "Moka Shako" and walk 20 minutes.
* From JR {{ill|Utsunomiya Station|Q801549|qid=Q801549}}, take the Kanto bus bound for “Utsunomiya Tobu-Moka Office” for about an hour, and get off at “Omae Jinja-mae”.
* Parking: Yes

He is said to be {{ill|Nuo folk religion|Q5371419|qid=Q5371419|lt=Hosoji}}, a descendant of {{ill|En no Gyōja|de|En no Gyōja|es|En no Gyōja|fa|ان نو گیوجا|fr|En no Gyōja|he|אן נו גיוג'ה|it|En no Gyōja|ja|役小角|ko|엔노 오즈누|pl|En-no Gyōja|ru|Эн-но Гёдзя|sh|En no Gyōja|uk|Ен-но-Ґьодзя|zh|役小角|qid=Q198946}}.: Exchanges with Omae Shrine occurred due to the appearance of the Hoso clan in the Oinashiki ceremony in 2017 (Heisei 29). |accessdate=2019-01-25 |publisher=Omae Shrine ~Walking with Shinto Faith~}}</ref>, On Setsubun in {{ill|2019|Q25274|qid=Q25274}} (Heisei 31), a goshuin stamp made with funds raised through crowdfunding was dedicated. As a result, goshuin stamps of Omae Shrine and Ashioyama Shrine (Bike Shrine) within the precincts were created and awarded for one month in February 2019. |title=[Kurafan] Let's make Setsubun Goshuin for Tsuina-chan and dedicate it to Omae Shrine❣️[Plan] |date=2018-10-24 |accessdate=2019-01-25 |work=Fantia [Onikko Hunter Tsuina-chan]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://ameblo.jp/oosakijinja/entry-12414527938.html |title=Tsuina-chan goshuin dedication project |date=2018-10-26 |accessdate=2019-01-25 |publisher=Omae Shrine ~Walking with Shinto faith~}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|url=https://ameblo.jp/oosakijinja/entry-12435182006.html |title=Current situation of cold red plum blossoms and Setsubun special goshuin |date=2019-01-24 |accessdate=2019-01-25 |publisher=Omae Shrine ~Walking with Shinto faith~}}</ref>.: In 2019 (Reiwa 1), a story set at Omae Shrine was created in the voice drama "Onikko Hunter Tsuina-chan". ! |date=2019-07-23 |accessdate=2019-11-01 |publisher=Omae Shrine ~Walking with Shinto Faith~}}</ref>.
